claim: 90 closed unit squares fit inside the closed axis-aligned square [0,L]^2 with pairwise disjoint interiors at the exact rational side in candidate.json.gz.

interpretation.triple: cx,cy,t where t=tan(theta/2), theta counterclockwise from positive x axis
interpretation.touching: allowed; wall and pair separation margins must be nonnegative exactly
interpretation.arithmetic: Python standard-library Fraction and arbitrary-precision integers; no floating point decisions or trigonometry

acceptance: Require n=90 and exactly 90 rational triples, positive finite rational L, strict rational-string grammar; malformed shape, duplicate JSON keys and nonfinite/float coordinates reject.
Independently check each constructed quadrilateral has four unit edges, adjacent orthogonality, exact area one and the declared center.
Check all four corners against all four walls: 1440 exact nonnegative inequalities.
For each of all 4005 unordered pairs compute projection intervals on all four normals u_i,v_i,u_j,v_j; accept the pair iff at least one oriented projection gap is >= 0.
Reconstruct edge normals from vertices (rather than treating input angles as proof of shape); record the strongest exact separation margin, selected axis and direction for every pair.
Run the same full feasibility check on input.json.gz; recompute metadata and signed scalar comparisons independently.

Check candidate transformation from input against the claimed common positive scale plus one translation, unchanged orientations and unchanged square sizes; characterize precision gain separately from claimed registered gain.

Use only the four old points supplied in previous-comparisons.json for a conditional fixed-orientation common-center-scale obstruction; do not claim to authenticate the old full witness or provenance.
Accept finite feasibility only if every required positive and negative control gives its predeclared outcome; any deviation is a failed review run.

scope_limitations: No lower bound or proof of global/local optimality.
No priority, credit, archive completeness, author identity, or historical solver execution claim.
Signed comparisons establish arithmetic against supplied scalar references only; external register state and leaderboard provenance remain unverified by this review.
A finite nonnegative separation certificate proves feasibility; it does not establish robustness to perturbation.
